action.action-desc: Ms. Slotkin (for herself and Mr. Joyce of Ohio) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs

form.official-title: To improve and expand the Solid Start program of the Department of Veterans Affairs, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Solid Start Act of 2020.

paragraph.text: In 2020, veterans continue to die by suicide at higher rates than civilians. Many of those veterans have no ties to the Department of Veterans Affairs, limiting the ability of the Department to help in times of crisis.

The first year after separating from the military is a critical time in the transition to civilian life for a member of the Armed Forces. Many changes occur during that transition, from career and location changes to shifts in financial circumstances and health care coverage.

section.text: It is the sense of Congress that the United States must strive to better serve members of the Armed Forces and veterans who are transitioning to civilian life by—

paragraph.text: providing up-to-date information and access to resources that such members of the Armed Forces may not be aware of;
supporting the critical time of transition by ensuring that mental health needs are met in a timely manner; and
assisting members of the Armed Forces and veterans in accessing newly available services.

section.text: The purposes of this Act are—

paragraph.text: to build the capacity of the Department of Veterans Affairs to efficiently and effectively respond to the queries and needs of veterans who have recently separated from the Armed Forces; and
to systemically integrate and coordinate efforts to assist veterans, including efforts—

subparagraph.text: to proactively reach out to newly separated veterans to—

clause.text: inform them of their eligibility for programs of and benefits provided by the Department; and
provide them information relating to the programs of, and benefits provided by, an appropriate veterans agency of a State; and

subparagraph.text: to connect veterans in crisis to resources that address their immediate needs.

section.header: Activities of the Solid Start program of the Department of Veterans Affairs

subsection.text: The Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, shall carry out the Solid Start program of the Department of Veterans Affairs by—

paragraph.text: collecting up-to-date contact information during transition classes or separation counseling for all members of the Armed Forces who are separating from the Armed Forces, while explaining the existence and purpose of the Solid Start program;
calling each veteran, regardless of separation type or characterization of service, not less than twice within the first year after separation from the Armed Forces;
providing information about the Solid Start program on the website of the Department and in materials of the Department, especially transition booklets and other resources;
providing information described in section 4(2) and ensuring calls are truly tailored to the needs of each veteran’s unique situation by conducting quality assurance tests; and
prioritizing outreach to veterans who have accessed mental health resources prior to separation from the Armed Forces.

subsection.text: The Secretary of Veterans Affairs, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, may carry out the Solid Start program by—

paragraph.text: encouraging members of the Armed Forces who are transitioning to civilian life to authorize alternate points of contact who can be reached should the member be unavailable during the first year following the separation of the member from the Armed Forces;
following up missed phone calls with tailored mailings to ensure the veteran still receives similar information; and
striving to reach out to veterans who separated prior to the initiation of the Solid Start program to provide similar services to those veterans, when feasible.

section.header: Assessment by Government Accountability Office of Solid Start program of the Department of Veterans Affairs

paragraph.text: Beginning on the date that is one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Comptroller General of the United States shall carry out an assessment of the Solid Start program of the Department of Veterans Affairs.
The assessment required by paragraph (1) shall analyze the following:

subparagraph.text: How many veterans have been contacted through the Solid Start program since the establishment of the program as compared to how many veterans have not been reached.
Whether feedback on the Solid Start program indicates that the program is working.
Whether the Solid Start program is meeting the purposes described in section 4.
Improvements that could be made to the Solid Start program.

subsection.text: Not later than 120 days after the date described in subsection (a)(1), the Comptroller General shall—

paragraph.text: complete the assessment required by such subsection; and
submit a report on the findings of the assessment to—

subparagraph.text: the Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the Committee on Armed Services of the Senate; and
the Committee on Veterans' Affairs and the Committee on Armed Services of the House of Representatives.

section.text: There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this Act the greater of—

paragraph.text: such sums as may be necessary for each fiscal year to carry out this Act; or
the amount expended by the Department of Veterans Affairs during fiscal year 2020 to carry out activities of the Solid Start program.
